title: Data Platform Engineer Pilot Playbook and Cost Safeguards
content:
## Overview
This playbook is a practical, sales-enabled guide designed for data platform and analytics engineering teams evaluating Redwood Inference as the inference layer for data products and ML pipelines. It combines positioning and messaging, competitor differentiation, an actionable pilot runbook, pitch-deck slide outline, pricing guardrails, two short case vignettes, and a security FAQ tailored for technical procurement conversations.

Audience: platform engineers, data platform leads, ML infrastructure owners, and solution architects.

Intent: enable a fast, low-risk pilot that demonstrates cost, latency, and operational improvements and creates a clear path to Dedicated or Private deployment.

Owner: Go-to-market enablement; technical ownership and supporting collateral maintained by Eng: Serving Runtime and Eng: Platform teams.

## Key positioning and messaging (elevator + technical hooks)
- Elevator (for engineers): "Redwood Inference lets your data platform serve production LLM features with predictable latency, clear unit economics, and controlled deployment options — from hosted API to private VPCs — without re-architecting pipelines."
- Value hooks for data platforms:
  - Predictable cost per inference through batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations.
  - Low-impact integration: standard REST/SDK endpoints and native connectors to existing feature stores and event streams.
  - Deployment flexibility: start hosted, move to Dedicated pools or Private VPC with identical APIs and metrics.
- Top technical proof points to emphasize in conversations:
  1. p95 latency guardrails and live sampling traces (Redwood Console per-route traces).
  2. Measured token-unit cost delta after applying batching + KV caching recommendations.
  3. Consistent model rollouts with canary and automatic fallback policies across environments.

## Competitive brief (concise)
- Competitor archetypes:
  - Managed LLM API providers: fastest to prototype but opaque unit economics and limited deployment modes.
  - Cloud-hosted model endpoints (general cloud providers): deep infra integration but higher operational burden for model orchestration and inference optimizations.
  - Self-hosted inference stacks: maximum control but slow to iterate and costly to maintain (engineering tax).

- Redwood differentiators for data platforms:
  - Unified serving API across hosted, dedicated, and private modes (same SDK + rollout semantics).
  - Cost-reduction toolkit (Redwood Optimize) with actionable quantization and batching recipes tuned per workload.
  - Routing and fallback policies that enable hybrid strategies (e.g., cheap-quantized variant for background workloads, high-fidelity variant for low-latency user-facing flows).

- Quick objection responses:
  - "We can self-host cheaper": Present estimated TCO including engineering time (runbook ops, kernel tuning, KV caching) and show 6–12 month break-even with Redwood Dedicated for steady-state throughput > 60k tokens/min.
  - "Security/compliance concerns": Highlight Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations (see Security FAQ below).

## Pilot definition (30–45 day technical sprint)
Goal: validate latency p95 < 200ms on representative queries, demonstrate >= 30% reduction in per-token cost vs naive hosted baseline using Redwood Optimize suggestions, and deploy a canary rollbackable route to production traffic.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- p50/p95 generation latency measured end-to-end and reported in Redwood Console.
- Token cost reduction target >= 30% during pilot window.
- Error rate < 0.5% and SLO breach days = 0.
- Business metric: reduction in user wait time or batch-processing wall time (customer-defined).

Pilot milestones (recommended cadence):
1. Week 0: Kickoff & environment access — identify pilot owner, allocate Redwood API keys, create an initial model route (hosted) with sample traffic replay.
2. Week 1: Baseline capture — run 72-hour traffic replay, capture latency, token counts, sequence-length distribution, and cold-cache behavior.
3. Week 2: Apply Redwood Optimize recommendations — enable batching, prefix caching, and one quantization profile; rerun replay.
4. Week 3: Integrate tracing + console dashboards; deploy canary route to 1% production traffic if safe.
5. Week 4–6: Iterate on model variant routing, autoscale policies; prepare handoff doc and decision brief to move to Dedicated/Private.

Roles & ownership:
- Customer: pilot owner (data platform engineer), data access, success metric definition.
- Redwood: solutions engineer (pre-sales lead), playbook author (GTM), runtime engineer for tuning support.
- Escalation contact: Redwood Solutions SE on-call (contact template in related pages).

Data collection checklist (deliverable):
- Latency traces (p50/p95), token counts, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates.
- Cost breakdown: raw token charges, networking, Redwood Optimize recommendations and projected savings.
- Failure modes: common error classes and example traces for triage.

## Pitch deck outline (10 slides — one-liner per slide)
1. Title & value proposition: accelerated inference for data platforms.
2. The problem: unpredictable inference cost and ops complexity for data products.
3. Why now: model proliferation + need for predictable serving.
4. Redwood overview: runtime + Optimize + Console + deployment modes.
5. Technical differentiation: batching, KV caching, routing, quantization profiles.
6. Pilot plan and success metrics (30–45 day runbook).
7. Economics: pilot budget, projected 6–12 month TCO scenarios.
8. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO checklist.
9. Case snapshots: two short examples demonstrating cost/latency wins.
10. Ask / next steps: pilot kickoff checklist, legal/contract runway, proposed resources.

Speaker notes: include a one-paragraph technical summary for slides 4–6 to help Sales Engineers answer rapid questions.

## Pricing guidance and cost safeguards
Pilot budget guidance:
- Typical pilot: $1k–$7k total consumption (hosted) depending on traffic replay volume and sequence lengths.
- Recommendation: cap hosted trial spend via API key quotas and rate limits; use per-route quotas in Redwood Console.

Rules of thumb:
- Short conversational generation (avg 50 tokens): expect lowest unit cost when using continuous batching and small-quantization variant for non-critical paths.
- Large sequence scoring (>= 1k tokens): prefer Dedicated pools or batch-job routes; estimate cost by tokens * model multiplier.

Negotiation levers to present to buying teams:
- Temporary pilot credit for qualified accounts (ask for Business Development approval).
- Committed Dedicated pool pricing with explicit burst allocation and rollback clauses.
- Performance SLAs for Dedicated deployments (p95 latency targets baked into contract).

Cost-safeguard checklist for pilots:
1. Set per-key daily spend limits.
2. Route non-user-facing workloads to quantized/cheaper variants.
3. Enable token-level sampling and early-exit heuristics for long-running generations.
4. Monitor Redwood Console alerts for unexpected token usage spikes and auto-disable routes.

## Short case vignettes (two concise examples)
1) Acero Health (synthetic vignette)
- Context: Acero needed an embeddings-based retrieval layer for clinical note summarization.
- Pilot outcome: 38% unit-cost reduction after enabling prefix caching and a conservative quantization profile; p95 latency reduced from 420ms to 160ms on user queries.
- Business outcome: Faster clinician turnaround and a path to Dedicated for PHI-scoped workflows.

2) Nimbus Commerce (synthetic vignette)
- Context: Real-time product feed enrichment for mobile shopping experiences.
- Pilot outcome: Canary rollout across 5% traffic validated fallbacks and reduced cold-start errors; overall inference spend for pilot was $2.6k and projected 44% savings at steady state with Dedicated capacity.
- Business outcome: Enabled feature launch and cost guardrails for scale.

## Security FAQ for prospect conversations (engineer-focused)
Q: Can Redwood run inside our VPC / on-prem environment?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a customer-controlled control plane with optional on-prem packaging. Networking and peering templates are available in the deployment guide (see related pages).

Q: How does key management work?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers and supports HSM-backed keys for model encryption and auditable key access. Keys can be rotated on your schedule.

Q: What kind of audit logging and traceability do you provide?
A: Per-request audit logs, per-route traces in Redwood Console, and optional long-term log export to customer S3/GCS/secure SIEM. We capture token counts and route identifiers but do not store plaintext inputs for customers who enable strict retention; retention settings are configurable.

Q: Can we limit data residency and retention?
A: Yes. Private deployments and regional Dedicated pools can enforce residency controls. Retention windows for logs and prompts are configurable (default 30 days; can be reduced).

Q: What certifications / evidence can we provide?
A: We provide SOC2 and ISO sensitivity statements, penetration-test reports under NDA, and a compliance pack for procurement. For higher assurance needs we offer engagement with our security team to produce tailored evidence bundles.

Q: How do you prevent model drift from hurting product quality after rollouts?
A: Redwood supports model versioning, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automated quality regression alerts tied to stored prompt sets and evals. Canary traffic can be routed with automatic rollback on metric degradation.

## Handover & next steps (operational)
- After pilot success, produce a 1-page decision brief with: measured p95/p50 latency, token cost delta, recommended deployment mode (Dedicated/Private), and proposed committed capacity.
- Sales: attach pilot evidence and a proposed term sheet with clear burst terms and an opt-out window.
- Eng Ongoing: schedule a 2-hour Knowledge Transfer session between Redwood runtime engineers and customer platform team to capture ops runbook and automation scripts.
